Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

the more …, the more … phrase

also the more the more, the more … the less, the less … the less, the sooner the better, so much the better, the bigger … the better

classical

Cic. Sen. 66: quō viae minus restet, eō plūs viāticī quaerere
Quint. 2.2.5: quō saepius monuerit, hōc rārius castīgābit

quō … eō (+ comparative)

construction: the ablative of the measure of difference in each half, each with its comparative; hōc may stand for eō

Each half has its own comparative, and the quō-clause usually comes first; the second half may have hōc for eō.

Other words

  • quantō … tantō (+ comparative) — the more …, the more … (by so much)

    construction: the same, with quantō and tantō · classical · Cic. Off. 1.90: quantō superiōrēs sīmus, tantō nōs gerāmus summissius; Liv. praef. 12: quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat

    Used just like quō … eō. Tantō alone is “so much the”: tantō melior, so much the better.

Examples

  • Quō citius vēneris, eō diūtius lūdēmus.

    The sooner you come, the longer we’ll play.composed

  • potest enim quicquam esse absurdius quam, quō viae minus restet, eō plūs viāticī quaerere?

    can anything be sillier than to look for more provisions the less road is left?Cic. Sen. 66

  • quō saepius monuerit, hōc rārius castīgābit

    the more often he warns, the less often he will punishQuint. 2.2.5

  • ut, quantō superiōrēs sīmus, tantō nōs gerāmus summissius

    that the higher we stand, the more humbly we should behaveCic. Off. 1.90

  • adeō quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat

    so true was it that the less wealth there was, the less greedLiv. praef. 12

  • sed quantō ille magis fōrmās sē vertet in omnēs, tantō, nāte, magis contende tenācia vincla

    but the more he turns himself into every shape, the tighter, my son, pull the binding cordsVerg. G. 4.411–412

  • quantō plūs propinquōrum, quantō major adfīnium numerus, tantō grātiōsior senectūs

    the more kinsmen, the greater the number of in-laws, the more honoured old age isTac. Germ. 20.5

  • tantō melior, surge et īnspīrā

    so much the better: get up and take a breathSen. Ep. 31.4

See also more, less, more, as … as, than, a lot, a little.
